source_facts.statement: dom f = {x | f(x) < +infinity}; this alone includes bottom.
Proper means no negative infinity anywhere and finite at at least one point.

lambda >= 0; proper f:R^d -> (-infinity,+infinity]; chosen norm; convex V subset dom f. For every x,y in V and 0<alpha<1, f(alpha*x+(1-alpha)*y) <= alpha*f(x)+(1-alpha)*f(y) - (lambda/2)*alpha*(1-alpha)*norm(x-y)^2.
Support characterization additionally uses convex V subset dom(partial f); quantified over all x,y in V and all g in partial f(y). Not required for the direct definition bridge.

A.1 integral route requires interior-domain points; A.3 attainment requires compact V, lower semicontinuity, Hausdorff ambient, and V intersect dom f nonempty. Neither licenses attainment on an arbitrary closed unbounded set.

interface.literal_source_domain: V subset effectiveDomain f, hence D=V intersect effectiveDomain f equals V. Do not silently replace the literal source set by a smaller D.
interface.precise_equivalence_candidate: For real normed E, f:E->EReal, global no-bottom, convex V, V subset effectiveDomain f, lambda>=0: the displayed source interior-weight inequality on V is equivalent to StrongConvexOn V lambda (fun x => (f x).toReal). SourceProper f is retained as source premise; a finite witness derives it when V is nonempty. This equivalence remains to be proved in Lean.
interface.coefficient: Mathlib UniformConvexOn subtracts a*b*(lambda/2*norm(x-y)^2); exactly the source lambda/2 after real multiplication reassociation.
interface.endpoints: Mathlib quantifies a,b>=0 with a+b=1. Interior a,b are alpha and 1-alpha; boundary a=0 or b=0 reduces to equality. Convex V and V subset dom f ensure all evaluated segment values are finite.
interface.ambient_delta: Arbitrary real normed spaces generalize source R^d with its chosen norm; no inner product, finite dimensionality or completeness is needed for the definitional bridge.
interface.general_D_route: For arbitrary V, D=V intersect effectiveDomain f can be used as an explicitly generalized finite-domain interface, provided Convex D and the necessary finite witness are independently supplied/derived. It is not equivalent to literal strong convexity on V unless V subset dom f (or a separately reviewed interpretation) is established.
interface.closed_top_outside: Closedness and top outside V are not Definition4.1 hypotheses. They may belong to later constrained algorithms; top outside V is harmless when every conversion is restricted to finite points in V. Closedness is not needed for the equivalence.
interface.proper_restriction: Ambient properness does not imply properness after restriction to V: f=indicator({0}), V={1} is proper closed convex ambient data but restricted function is everywhere top. Require an actual finite point in V.
interface.no_totalization: Never infer extended strong convexity from unrestricted toReal. Top and bottom map to zero; constant-top f on a singleton has a vacuous real strong-convex inequality for every lambda but is not proper. No-bottom plus domain membership are required at endpoints and segment.
